newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to end free 5-hour offer of WorldNet.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to end free 5-hour offer of WorldNet.

text.p: AT&T Corp said that it will end its introductory offer to its long distance customers of five free hours a month of its WorldNet Internet access service on March 31 and it will begin a revised hourly pricing plan.
AT&T said WorldNet will continue to offer its unlimited usage pricing plan of $19.95 a month, citing customer demand and its ability to support this pricing through its network.
Starting March 31, AT&T will offer its long distance customers who sign up for the WorldNet service and anticipate lower usage a monthly rate of $4.95 for their first five hours.
Long distance customers who signed up before March 31 will continue to receive their first five hours for free for one year and they will be enrolled in the revised pricing when their year ends.

Customers of long distance carriers other than AT&T can receive the service for $4.95 for the first three hours. All hourly plan customers pay $2.50 for each additional hour, and pay separately for telephone access or 800 number access to reach the service (taxes and other charges may apply).
AT&T said its introductory offer of five free hours to its long distance customers brought many new users to the Internet.

AT&T also is offering an incentive to its hourly users to switch over to its flat rate plan. Customers on the hourly pricing plan as of March 2 who see that their Internet usage is growing will receive their third month of the unlimited $19.95 a month plan for free if they trade up by April 30.
Beginning June 1, if customers leave at any time, AT&T will forward their electronic mail to their new service free for 60 days.
AT&T also said it began posting statistics about the reliability and performance of WorldNet and it challenged other service providers to match AT&T's performance.
AT&T said it will regularly report reliability figures for AT&T WorldNet on its main home page on the Internet and on the AT&T WorldNet Service home page.

AT&T said it has retained Inverse Network Technology Inc, an independent company that measures the performance of Internet service providers, to measure the average percentage of customers who successfully dial into the service on their first try. Results are tracked and reported over a rolling 14-day period and compared with an industry average.
For example, for the most recent period, the success rate of getting online was 93.5 percent for AT&T WorldNet members.

This compares with an industry average of 86.8 percent. During peak Internet usage time, (6 pm to midnight local time), the success rates were 87.1 percent for AT&T WorldNet compared to an indudstry average of 79.1 percent.
AT&T currently has more than 750,000 members and it said it is the largest pure Internet access provider in the U.S.

America Online Inc, which has been having massive congestion problems as its members swamped the service when it switched to flat-rate pricing, is the world's largest online service, with eight million members.
